components: a wide curve that rises along the top, rounds the right side and sweeps away to the lower left
strokeOrder: draw the short top stroke from left to right
lift, begin at the left and rise to the right along the top, then without lifting curve down round the right side and sweep away to the lower left
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03046 file records う as two stroke paths in this order and direction: the short top stroke, then the wide curve; so there is one pen lift.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03046.svg, hiragana う (U+3046 HIRAGANA LETTER U), two stroke paths kvg:03046-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the short top stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts at the left, rises to the right along the top, rounds the right side and sweeps away to the lower left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.

notes: After と it writes a long o, as in ありがとう.
